correctness.rationale: For each cyclic stabilizer quotient the unique chosen base generator has order equal to the orbit index. The packet conditions are exactly graph independence, so the minimum packet count is the chromatic number. Unique edge primes and vertex-private primes give a squarefree cyclic action realizing any graph with distinct orbit types. The equivariant unit group is a direct product of cyclic quotients with Sylow rank at most two, exactly two when the graph has an edge. The reduction uses polynomially many polynomial-size primes and binary indices; membership in NP is by gcd checking. The included checker independently tests all 1099 graphs of order up to five and the 900-element explicit group; finite testing is not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 preprint and final journal article introduce coprime packet merging, but leave exact packet optimization open and do not derive graph universality, NP-completeness, or a two-generator unbounded gap. The 2022/2023 theorem concerns a different relative-rank invariant. Relevant published-finding corpus searches found no covering statement. Universal intersection graphs, finite-abelian-group rank and 3-coloring hardness are prior ingredients, not independently claimed. Some unindexed literature and one inaccessible related record remain risks.
residual_risks: The 2026 packet invariant is generator-choice-dependent outside the cyclic setting; no assertion extends to noncyclic groups.
The NP-completeness statement is for compressed orbit indices; the same hardness is not claimed for explicit action tables.
Some older or unindexed sources could contain the prime-index action realization in another language.
The related published wreath-product relative-rank record had only summary material accessible; its full text was not used for a whole-document noncoverage assertion.

value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly identifies the packet number as a target for structural determination. Here all finite graphs occur as cyclic-action packet conflicts, showing NP-complete optimization even over squarefree cyclic groups with binary orbit data. The same construction keeps the actual equivariant automorphism group two-generated, while optimal packets range without bound. This gives a genuine computational boundary and a sharp structural separation for the source’s generator optimization, not a gratuitous numerical subcase.
